title: Наказание в больнице и мясной секрет  (Hospital Punishment and the Meat Secret)

segments.t: Returned to his hospital bed, Chef Barinov is scolded by the nurse for climbing out the window and driving his blood pressure up. When Vika arrives to visit the supposedly weak patient, she catches him happily devouring smuggled meat with a huge appetite.
Я вечером загляну еще, сейчас чайку вам принесу.
Я все уже знаю, я к вам приеду.
Let's replay the exchange and look closely at each Russian phrase.
'Alright then, get some rest.' Max anchors the line on 'come on', while 'rest' completes the thought.
'Get some rest. Albert Igorevich?' Notice how Russian expresses 'rest' and 'Igorevich' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Max answers right away.
'We need to stabilize your blood pressure.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'blood pressure' before landing on 'to settle'.
'Climbing out the window like that.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'how' before landing on 'little window'.
'I am begging you, please.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'I' and finishing on 'beg'. Sasha answers right away.
Я вечером загляну еще, сейчас чайку вам принесу.
'I will check in again this evening, and right now I will bring you some tea.' The meaning hinges on 'I' working together with 'will bring' in spoken Russian.
'How are things going with you?' Notice how Russian expresses 'things' and 'you' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
'Detained while attempting to escape.' Notice how Russian expresses 'has been detained' and 'flight' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Max answers right away.
Я все уже знаю, я к вам приеду.
'I already know everything, I will come visit you.' The grammar packs 'I' and 'to arrive' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'What should I bring you?' In Russian, the idea of 'what' flows naturally into 'for you' without extra filler words.
'Running and jumping around.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'runs around' before landing on 'to jump'. Sasha answers right away.
'He is eating with such an appetite.' The grammar packs 'he' and 'there is' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'Learn the Russian language first.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'Russian' and finishing on 'to learn'. Let's hear the complete conversation once more.
Я вечером загляну еще, сейчас чайку вам принесу.
Я все уже знаю, я к вам приеду.
